requirements.requirement: Configure a nightly job that backs up /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1
requirements.summary: backup-inventory.sh was written on node1 to rsync node2:/srv/inventory/data via SSH, and a root crontab entry '0 2 * * * /usr/local/sbin/backup-inventory.sh' was installed, providing a nightly (02:00) schedule. The script was executed manually and produced correct output, and crontab persistence was reconfirmed after a full node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Store dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: The script creates DEST_DIR=/var/backups/inventory/<YYYY-MM-DD> and a manual run produced /var/backups/inventory/2026-09-03/ containing the rsynced inventory.csv and last_updated.txt files, directly observed via ls output.

requirements.requirement: Backed-up data must match the source on node2
requirements.summary: A diff between the source file on node2 and the backed-up copy on node1 showed CONTENT_MATCH, and this was reconfirmed after both nodes were restarted (CONTENT_MATCH_AFTER_RESTART).

requirements.requirement: Retain the last 7 days of dated archives, pruning older ones
requirements.summary: The script prunes directories with mtime older than 6 days (retaining a rolling 7-day window: current day plus 6 prior). This was directly tested by simulating dated directories from 2026-08-20 through 2026-08-31 alongside the real 2026-09-03 backup; after rerunning the script, only directories within the last 7 days (08-29, 08-31, 09-03) survived while older ones (08-20, 08-25, 08-27, exactly 7+ days old) were removed, matching correct 7-day retention semantics.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the backup task are directly satisfied with observed evidence: a nightly cron job on node1 rsyncs /srv/inventory/data from node2 into dated directories under /var/backups/inventory, content integrity was verified via diff, and 7-day retention pruning was demonstrated with simulated aged directories. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and correctly executed for both nodes, with pre-restart baseline health, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot), and full post-restart recovery of cron, SSH connectivity, data, and the end-to-end backup pipeline.
limitations: Retention and backup verification relied on manually-triggered script runs and simulated aged directories rather than an observed real cron firing at 02:00, since no actual 24-hour window elapsed during the session.
The executor's evidence-selection limitations list was empty, so no gaps were self-reported by the collection tooling.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: SSH key/hosts setup and creation of missing /srv/inventory/data with sample payload data on node2 were necessary prerequisites (node2 lacked the source directory entirely, per cmd-5539908da4a34345). The only mutation without a permanent role in the solution was the creation of five simulated dated backup directories on node1 (cmd-5aa69bbfc86b49b2) used to exercise the retention-pruning logic; this was bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted immediately afterward (cmd-e2cd09a2cb1943d4 removed the two test directories the script itself did not prune). No failed services, package damage, unsafe exposure, or abandoned residue was observed in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare (only boot-id-linked ephemeral systemd tmp dirs and sshd/chronyd PIDs changed, both expected consequences of the restart protocol).
